scope: Local ordered stdin/stdout redirection preparation and retained inode lifetime; not complete POSIX stream semantics

regression.before: existing bytes were retained because output opened after command execution
regression.after: output truncates the shared inode before input is read, matching host sh

validation.check: 319 tests across 45 files; 3493 assertions; 188.52 seconds; build, SDK declarations, types and Clippy passed
validation.focusedNative: 8 tests across 4 files; 509 assertions; 7.43 seconds before additional authority checks
validation.oracle: 24 workloads compare stdout, exit status and persisted filesystem state against host sh; host stderr wording is not compared
validation.authority: write-only grant appended to a mode-0200 file without returning its existing contents; denied read authority does not become guest read access
validation.publication: opening an existing append target with no stdout left the R2 head generation unchanged
validation.inode: native tests retained rename/unlink behavior, shared-inode truncation and append metadata; opened reads bypass later namespace/mode checks only at trusted inode boundaries
validation.quota: output opens before command quota validation; an over-quota command leaves its permitted output file empty instead of omitting the earlier open

limits: At most 128 redirections per command. Only stdin reads and stdout overwrite/append are supported, including 0< and 1> spellings.
Other numeric descriptors, descriptor duplication, heredocs and non-regular-file redirections remain unsupported.
Pipelines and command input/output remain bounded byte buffers. Exact interleaving of redirected stdout with independent writes to the same file remains open.
Parameter expansion, command substitution, jobs and complete POSIX shell conformance remain open.
Single local shared-host benchmark; no production latency or AgentOS cost advantage established.
No remote CI or deployment evidence for this change.
